name: Camo Green
lede: Camo Green is a muted olive-green from the X11 and CSS color keyword list, close enough to Dark Olive Green that Wikipedia records the two within 2.5 CIEDE2000 units of each other.

sections.title: A web keyword with a near-twin
sections.body:
Wikipedia's "List of colors" cites the X11/Web standard as its source, and our library finds the xkcd survey's version of the same cluster essentially unchanged [1]. The name describes camouflage patterning generically, not any single military fabric or dye [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[army-green]], [[military-green]], [[velvet-green]] and [[mud]], at 3.1, 5.9, 
Its closest learnable match is [[hunter-green|Hunter green]], about 11 units off in CIEDE2000, a reminder that "camo green" sits at the darker, duller edge of the green family [1]. Family neighbors are [[olive]], [[hunter-green|Hunter green]], and [[khaki]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this olive in 121 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.5 percent, as photographed [2]. [[painter:vincent-van-gogh|Van Gogh]] carries it at 12 times the archive's rate and Edvard Weie at nearly 24 times; the earliest dated hit is a 1420 Crucifixion scene, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

It covers the most canvas in George Inness's *After a Summer Shower* (1894), followed by a Danish woodland study from 1847 [2]. United States paintings carry it 3.5 times the archive average [2]. These are computed color matches on aged, varnished photographs, not pigment identifications [2].
